feeling overwhelmed by the news? here is a tip to cut the number of articles you read without being any less informed.quickly skim the summary or opening paragraph for keywords indicating a future tense. "will be", "soon" "next week" and skip them. if the event promised or predicted actually happens you will get to read that article and perhaps dozens more about the aftereffects. on the other hand most of the future cast stories are just filler in the news hole.example: politician does the cable news circuit talking about what they will do, a bill they plan to introduce, etc. unless you are in the drafting process you don't have to care, it is usually just talk anyway and nothing will actually happen. if it is actually introduced you might want to post or write letters in support or opposition but some moron blathering about what they might or might not do "later" isn't news you can use.same for all these scandals. every day we get "kabooms!" that don't really mean anything yet, the stories are all about "shocking reveal" coming soon that will mean something later. not news you can use because later never comes. if "later" eventually comes, that is news you need to read and care about.seriously. mike lindell released "absolute proof" how long ago? raise your hand if you watched it. but everybody is still pushing "kaboom!" stories every day about the "shocking new evidence soon to be revealed that will change everything." so the "absolute proof" wasn't in fact absolute? yeah, the math was incontrovertible. didn't matter. but they have news cycles to fill, podcasts to grind out, etc.tune them out and get back a lot of time for self improvement. or time to figure out an actual game plan instead of this current delay and pacification campaign.
